summary: Staging surcharge line item appears on prod invoice and credit applied to wrong legal entity after org migration
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a surcharge labeled 'staging-environment-fee' on their March invoice (INV-2026-03-HELIOS) even though the organization migrated to a consolidated production billing entity on 2026-03-02. Impact: Invoice balance increased by $4,120.45 USD and a credit memo of -$3,950.00 USD was issued to a different legal entity (Helios Labs LLC) causing a small outstanding balance and a mismatch in accounts receivable. Environment: prod-us-east; customer uses dedicated capacity and has multiple subaccounts that were consolidated in the org migration. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run billing export for INV-2026-03-HELIOS 2) Observe line item 'staging-environment-fee' with SKU billing:staging_surcharge 3) Note credit memo CM-2026-03-875 applied to Helios Labs LLC instead of Helios Analytics, Inc. 4) Verify org migration log: migration-job-2026-03-02-0x7a 5) Check usage post-migration: no active staging keys after 2026-03-02 Logs/IDs: invoice INV-2026-03-HELIOS, credit CM-2026-03-875, migration job migration-job-2026-03-02-0x7a, billing export run: billing-export-2026-03-11-02z. Customer note: They require the credit to be re-applied to the billed legal entity and a corrected invoice for accounting reconciliation. They are awaiting a manual credit memo and confirmation for their finance team by COB 2026-03-12.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Maya Chen: Opened with customer after they uploaded invoice PDF. Customer says charge appears to be for staging usage that should have been zeroed during migration.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Darius Patel: Assigned to billing ops to triage. Requested export of invoice ledger and migration logs. Asked finance to hold collection until we confirm resolution.

2026-03-10 13:18 - Billing Ops (Elena R.): Pulled invoice INV-2026-03-HELIOS and found staging_surcharge 1 line for $4,120.45 USD and a manual credit CM-2026-03-875 for -$3,950.00 USD applied to Helios Labs LLC. Noted tax rounding difference of $12.10. Added linked runbook and flagged for engineering because credit attribution looks like a mapping failure in org-mapper service.

2026-03-11 08:44 - Eng SRE (Omar N.): Found a race in the migration-job where temporary staging namespaces were not swept before invoice snapshot generation. There is an HMAC mismatch that caused the charge to retain 'staging' SKU in the exported line items. Also found that credit application flow reads legal_entity_id from pre-migration cache when applying legacy credits.

2026-03-11 15:05 - Maya Chen: Notified customer of findings, told them we will issue a correcting credit memo to the correct legal entity and reissue a corrected invoice. Customer requested a clear AP description and the original credit to be reversed from Helios Labs LLC to avoid double counting in their ledgers.

2026-03-12 09:30 - Finance (Liam M.): Created manual credit CM-2026-03-900 for -$3,950.00 USD to Helios Analytics, Inc. Created reversal journal for CM-2026-03-875 and flagged collections hold. Preparing corrected invoice D-CORR-INV-2026-03-HELIOS-P1.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: billing snapshot included temporary staging namespace rows due to migration-job ordering; this produced a surcharge line on main invoice.
Verified billing export: staging_surcharge SKU present in invoice export with event timestamps 2026-03-02T03:12:44Z - this aligns with migration window.
Mapped credit CM-2026-03-875 to legal_entity_id 0x9b2 (Helios Labs LLC) from legacy cache; expected mapping to 0x4d7 (Helios Analytics, Inc.).
Found code path in org-mapper v2.1.3 where fallback_to_pre_migration_id = true when migration lock was present; this explains attribution to legacy entity.
Edge case: tax calculation module applied rounding after credit application resulting in $12.10 residual that must be handled with minor adjustment or consolidated memo.
Repro steps created and added to GH issue gh/infra/billing-fix/724 for a targeted fix: ensure migration snapshot is gated after sweep and disable fallback mapping during credit application window.
Observed no evidence of duplicate token metering or embedding overcount; usage lines other than the surcharge are normal.

Estimated customer monetary impact: invoice increased by $4,120.45; manual credit required $3,950.00 moved; remaining residual ~ $182.55 which includes tax/rounding; final adjustment will be documented in corrected invoice.
resolution: Temporary remediation: Finance issued reversal for CM-2026-03-875 and created CM-2026-03-900 applying credit to correct legal entity. Collections placed on hold for INV-2026-03-HELIOS.

Corrective actions taken: 1) Billing team generated corrected invoice D-CORR-INV-2026-03-HELIOS-P1 and marked original as replaced. 2) Engineering patched org-mapper to prevent fallback_to_pre_migration_id during credit runs (PR gh/infra/billing-fix/724 merged). 3) Migration runbook updated to include a sweep-and-confirm stage before invoice snapshot lock. 4) Added a small residual adjustment credit of -$182.55 to reconcile rounding (CM-2026-03-901).

Follow-up: Finance to confirm with customer that corrected invoice and credit memos meet AP requirements. Engineering to monitor next billing cycle exports for similar artifacts. Ticket will remain open until customer confirms and accounting closes reconciliation (target close date 2026-03-16).

Customer-facing message prepared: apologized, explained root cause (migration snapshot race + legacy mapping fallback), summarized fix and credits applied, provided accounting artifacts (INV replacement, CM numbers), and offered an incident postmortem if they want one.
